neighbours.label: a unit of measure right after a number (miles, kilometers, gallons, degrees Fahrenheit)
fire: The comet will pass Earth at a distance of roughly 4,500 miles next Tuesday.
Engineers said the new reservoir can store about 900 gallons of rainwater.
During the test the engine casing climbed to 900 degrees Fahrenheit.
The rover has now driven more than 28 kilometers across the crater floor.
Each tanker truck carries roughly 9,000 gallons of diesel to the station.
The spacecraft orbits the moon at an altitude of 62 miles.
Summer highs in the valley regularly reach 115 degrees Fahrenheit.
The new pipeline will stretch nearly 1,200 kilometers to the coast.
quiet: The comet will pass Earth at a distance that astronomers call close next Tuesday.
Engineers said the new reservoir can supply about 900 homes with rainwater.
During the test the engine casing glowed bright orange for a few seconds.
The rover has now taken more than 28 photographs of the crater floor.
Each tanker truck carries a driver and a trainee to the station.
The spacecraft orbits the moon with 3 instruments switched on.
Summer highs in the valley regularly break records set in 1915.
The new pipeline will employ nearly 1,200 workers along the coast.

notes: Card: ' miles' x9, ' kilometers' x5, ' Fahrenheit' x3, ' gallons', currency 'HUF' - all units following a numeral, mostly in space-science text. Probe: units after numbers 0.23-0.34; same number with a non-unit noun ~0.02.
